description: August 1 birthday meaning: Leo decan 1, birthday number 1, Life Path by year, Chinese zodiac note and famous birthdays.
answer: In Western astrology, an August 1 birthday falls in Leo, in the first decan, with Sun as the sign's ruler and Sun as the decan's. In numerology the day gives birthday number 1. The Life Path also uses the birth year. Leo is fixed and fire.

sections.heading: August 1 zodiac sign and personality
paragraphs: August begins with a doubled solar note: Leo, nine degrees in, sitting in the Sun's own decan, with birthday number 1, the most self-directed number. Traditional readings describe a natural lead, confident, creative and keen to make a mark. The most rewarding version of this birthday uses its spotlight to lift other people as well.

On August 1 the Sun usually sits at about 9° Leo, in the first decan, where Sun rules the decan as well as the sign. With the Sun ruling both the sign and its first decan, late-July birthdays sit in the most radiant part of Leo. This is traditionally the decan of presence: warmth, self-expression and a natural pull towards the centre of the stage or the head of the table. Generosity and loyalty are often strong, and so is a need to be appreciated for the effort behind the performance. The doubled solar tone can tip into wounded pride when recognition is withheld. These Lions usually shine brightest when their light is used to warm a whole group rather than only to illuminate themselves.

sections.heading: August 1 in numerology
paragraphs: Born on the 1st, your birthday number is a plain 1, with no compound behind it. In Pythagorean numerology the day of birth is a secondary number, a talent or flavour that sits alongside the Life Path rather than replacing it. A first-of-the-month birthday is traditionally read as the purest form of initiative: a self-starting streak, a preference for making decisions personally and a comfort with going first. Because there is nothing to reduce, the energy is often described as direct and uncomplicated. The usual counsel is to pair that independence with listening, so leadership does not become lonely.

The Life Path, the main number in a numerology chart, also uses the birth year, so it changes from one August 1 birthday to the next: it is 7 for 1960, 8 for 1970, 9 for 1980 and 1 for 1990, for example. Some birth years on this date reach the master number 11.

sections.heading: Born on August 1: season, famous birthdays and Chinese zodiac
paragraphs: An August birthday falls in late northern summer, a season of early harvests and holidays, and in late winter for the southern hemisphere, when the first blossom starts to appear. Leo holds most of the month, with Virgo arriving around August 22 or 23. August is month 8 in numerology, associated with ambition, authority and material skill, a fitting partner for Leo's confidence. August 1 is the 213rd day of the year (214th in a leap year). By August 23, 22 days later, the Sun has usually moved on into Virgo.

For the Chinese zodiac, Lunar New Year has always passed by August 1, so the animal is simply the one for the birth year. Well-known people born on August 1 include Herman Melville (1819), Jean-Baptiste de Lamarck (1744) and Abdullah of Saudi Arabia (1924).

faq.question: What zodiac sign is August 1?
faq.answer: August 1 is Leo in every year from 1930 to 2030, wherever you were born. It falls in the first decan of Leo, which tradition links with Sun.

faq.question: What is the Life Path number for someone born on August 1?
faq.answer: It depends on the birth year. On August 1 the Life Path is 7 in 1960, 8 in 1970, 9 in 1980, 1 in 1990, 11 in 2000, 3 in 2010 and 4 in 2020. The birthday number, from the day alone, is 1 for everyone born on the 1st.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac sign is someone born on August 1?
faq.answer: Chinese astrology is straightforward for an August 1 birthday: the new year began weeks earlier, so the birth year's own animal applies.

faq.question: Which famous people were born on August 1?
faq.answer: August 1 is also the birthday of Herman Melville (1819), Jean-Baptiste de Lamarck (1744) and Abdullah of Saudi Arabia (1924). The list comes from Wikidata and favours people with the most Wikipedia articles.
